question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, notice that
$\frac{8}{7}-\frac{1}{16}$
is not zero. Any non-zero number raised to the power of $0$ equals $1.$ So, we have 

$$
{(\frac{8}{7}-\frac{1}{16})}^{0}=1.
$$

Next, we evaluate the negative exponent and get

$$
{(\frac{1}{2})}^{-3}={(\frac{2}{1})}^{3}={2}^{3}=8.
$$

Substituting all these values into the expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{8}{7}-\frac{1}{16})}^{0}-11\times {(\frac{1}{2})}^{-3} & = \\ 1-11\times 8 & = \\ 1-88 & = \\ -87\end{aligned}
$$
